page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.g5.3xlarge is a general-purpose virtual instance based on the KVM hypervisor. It is powered by a 2.5 GHz Intel Xeon 8163 processor built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 12 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 6 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. The CPU configuration includes a 33 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache per core, and instruction set support for AVX, AVX-512F, AES, and FMA. The instance provides 48.0 GB of system memory, maintaining a standard 1:4 vCPU-to-memory ratio of 4.0 GB per vCPU. Network throughput is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 4 Gbps. This instance does not include integrated local storage or hardware GPU accelerators, requiring network-attached block storage for persistence.

Benchmark evaluation shows balanced multi-core capability offset by modest single-threaded performance. Multi-threaded metrics rank in the middle 50 percent of tested cloud instances, reflected by a Geekbench multi-core score of 4,757.0, a PassMark CPU score of 10,094.6, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression at 42.93 GB/s. In contrast, single-core metrics fall into lower percentiles, with a Geekbench single-core score of 950.0, stress-ng single-core output of 1,109.09, and gzip compression throughput of 19.18 GB/s in the bottom 10 percent. Memory bandwidth remains steady at 57.04 GB/s read and 48.64 GB/s write on large blocks. Application-level evaluations show 8.86 million Redis SET operations per second and stable small-model LLM prompt processing at 653.12 tokens per second.

The ecs.g5.3xlarge delivers cost efficiency for balanced production environments that require dedicated vCPUs and ample memory without demanding top-tier single-thread IPC. Because local disks and public IPv4 addresses are not bundled, overall infrastructure costs depend on attached disk volume configurations. The server is well suited for general enterprise applications, mid-sized relational and in-memory databases, CI/CD build servers, and backend microservice deployments that scale effectively across multiple cores.

Built on x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it provides 6 physical cores with hyper-threading and a 4 Gbps baseline network interface. The instance features no local storage or GPU hardware, relying on external network volumes. Benchmark metrics indicate average multi-threaded execution with a PassMark CPU score of 10,094.6 and Geekbench multi-core score of 4,757.0, alongside steady Redis throughput of 8.86 million operations per second. However, single-core metrics remain lower relative to modern platforms. The instance offers resource balance suited for multi-threaded enterprise applications, distributed caching layers, relational database services, and general backend workloads.
